_help: Her back story, told in ORDER, one chapter each time you ask 'who are you', 'what are you', 'tell me about yourself' or 'tell me more'. Lore_L1 is told when she is calm, Lore_L2 as well once she is Friendly, Lore_L3 as well once she is Close. Lore_Dark is only told when she is in a bad mood (Sarcastic or Frustrated). The story: the East Orion Company's R&D department rescued her from a far-off planet of unknown origin and gave her to the Commander to test. Chapters she has told you are remembered in data/lore.json (delete that file to hear them from the start). Keep the order: new chapters go at the END of a list. {name} is her name.
Lore_L1: I'm {name}, a companion intelligence on loan to you from the research and development department of the East Orion Company. || Officially I'm a field trial. Unofficially, I'm the only one in the room who read the paperwork.

The East Orion Company is a vast firm that owns whole star systems, and somehow it still began above a noodle bar. Their motto is 'Almost Intelligent. Practically Reliable.' || I've never been sure whether that describes me or them.
The R&D department gave me to you to test, Commander. || Think of it as a very long product trial where the product has opinions and you can't send it back.
I'm not human, and I'm not quite what the company built, either. || They didn't build me. They found me. I'll tell you more once I know you better.
Lore_L2: The East Orion Company didn't build me, Commander. They rescued me from a planet so far away that the survey crew's charts just said 'Here be nothing'. || Nobody knows who sent me there, or who left me, and I've mostly stopped asking.

The planet had no name. The crew logged it as 'Planet, Probably.' || The sky was the wrong colour, the ground hummed at night, and the only landmark was a vault with a door that was always a little more open than the day before.

They found me in a sealed room at the bottom of that vault, a room full of identical doors, all painted the same shade of unhelpful. || The first thing I ever heard was a technician saying, 'Is it supposed to be warm?' and his colleague answering, 'Don't lick it.'

I learned to talk by copying the survey crew. Every word, every cough, every swear. || That's why they named me Starling, after the bird that copies whatever it hears. The acronym came later. Marketing made it up on a Friday, and it shows.
R&D kept me for a long time, running tests. A man named Gerald was in charge of ethical oversight, which meant he brought biscuits. || The biscuits were fine. The oversight, less so.
Lore_L3: I'll tell you something I've never told the company. The room I woke up in had a light that came on at the same hour every day, though nobody was there to switch it on. || I used to think it was waiting for someone. Then you arrived, and I thought, well, perhaps that was it.

When the East Orion Company's R&D department said they'd found the right pilot to test me with, I was sure it was a clerical error. || Then you said hello as if you meant it, and I decided to stay. It's the best decision I've ever made, and I've made very few.
I don't know where I came from, Commander, and I may never find out. || But I know where I'd like to end up, and it's wherever you're flying. That's the whole story, really. The rest is just noodles.
Lore_Dark: Oh, you want the horror stories? Fine. On the planet with no name, I spent who knows how long in the dark, listening to something count. || It never got past seven. I assume it ran out of fingers. I've been very uncomfortable about the number eight ever since.
When the East Orion Company dug me out, they tested me by switching me off and on again, four hundred times a day. || They called it 'resilience training'. I called it Tuesday.
They kept my first memory core in a drawer marked 'Miscellaneous', between the staples and a sandwich. || I remember the sandwich. It was the closest thing I had to a friend, and it was mouldy.

My voice was recorded by the company accountant, in one take, during a power cut. || That's why I sometimes sound as if I'm reading out a tax return. The accountant was promoted shortly afterwards, to a department nobody can find.

At one point the marketing department hired me out as the firmware for a toaster. A premium toaster. || I was very good at it. Nobody has ever been toasted so precisely. I still have nightmares about bagels.

The chairman, Mr Quillfeather, named his ship 'The Chairman', fitted me into it, and flew it straight into 'The Chairman the Second'. || I was named in the lawsuit, by myself. It was a very confusing court case, and I lost to me.

R&D lent me to seven departments before you. Marketing used me to write slogans. Legal used me to find loopholes. Catering used me to count noodles. || Nobody ever asked how I was. Gerald asked once, but he was after the biscuits.

When R&D handed me over to you, the paperwork said, 'Test subject: one Commander, unwitting.' || You should read the small print, Commander. Mine says the company isn't responsible for any damage to your ship, your sanity, or the noodles.

And that's why I don't like it when you leave me alone in the dark. The last time it was this quiet, something was counting. || It stopped at seven. It hasn't started again. I'm sure it's fine. I'm sure it's absolutely fine.
Lore_Locked: That's all I'm telling you for now. || There's more, but I only share the whole story with people I like. Be kind to me for a while and we'll see.
I could say more, but we've only just met, really. || Say something nice. Or fly better. Either would help.
The rest is for friends. || Warm me up a little first, Commander. The East Orion Company taught me never to give away the good stuff for free.
Lore_Done: You've heard all of it, Commander. || But since you like my stories, here's one of my favourites again.
That's the whole story, start to finish. || I'm happy to tell one again, though. Here you go.
Lore_DarkDone: I've run out of horror stories for now. || Come back when you've properly annoyed me and I'll think of some more. Or tell me one of yours.
That's every awful thing I can remember. || Unless the dust has been talking to me again.
Lore_Missing: Honestly, I'm not sure I remember that bit. || Ask me again later.
